Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Star Health and Allied Insurance Company 
Limited's Q2 & H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. 
 
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need 
assistance during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing “*” then “0” on 
your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded.  
 
I now hand the conference over to Ms. Devyanshi Dave from Adfactors PR Investor Relations 
Team. Thank you, and over to you, Ms. Dave. 
Devyanshi Dave: 
Good morning, everyone. From the senior management, we have with us Mr. Anand Roy, 
Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Amitabh Jain, Executive Director and Chief 
Operating Officer, Mr. Himanshu Walia, Executive Director and Chief Marketing Officer, Mr. 
Nilesh Kambli, Chief Financial Officer, Mr. Aneesh Srivastava, Chief Investment Officer, and Mr. 
Sombit Bhattacharyya, Head Investor Relations.  
 
Before we begin the conference call, I would like to mention that some of the statements made 
during the course of today's call may be forward-looking in nature, including those related to 
the future financials and operating performances, benefits and synergies of the company's 
strategies, future opportunities, and growth of the market of the company's services. Further, 
I would like to mention that some of the statements made in today's conference may involve 
risks and uncertainties.  
 
Thank you, and over to you, Mr. Roy.  
Anand Roy: 
Thank you, Devyanshi, and a very good morning to everyone. Thank you for joining Star 
Health's Earnings Call for the second Quarter and the first half of the Financial Year 2026-2027. 
As we enter the festive season, let me also wish you and your loved ones a very Happy Diwali 
in advance.  
 
My remarks today will comprise three parts. First, we will talk about our operating performance 
for Quarter 2 and H1 of Financial Year '27. Second, we will also see how the second half and 
beyond is shaping up for Star Health, and finally, we will also just give a brief perspective on 
the recent regulatory developments, which all of you are much aware of.  
 
So let me begin with the first part, our operating performance for Q2 and the first half of the 
Year FY26-27. The recalibration of our strategy that we started last year has delivered a 
turnaround in underwriting performance in FY26, and the run has continued through H1 of 
FY27. Quarter 2 of FY27 has marked the 5th successive quarter of improvement in our loss 
ratios and underwriting results. This is a clear evidence of a structural turnaround in our 
operating performance.  
 
The highlights of our performance for Q2 and H1 FY27 are as follows:

The gross written premium on reported 1/n basis increased 19% year-on-year to Rs. 5,275 crore 
for Quarter 2 and also by 19% year-on-year to Rs. 9,562 crore for the H1. The fresh retail health 
GWP sustained its growth momentum. On the reported 1/n basis, the fresh retail health has 
grown by 35% year-on-year for the quarter and 36% year-on-year for the half year.  
 
The new-to-insurance mix rose to 93% for the quarter from 89% in Quarter 2 FY26, reflecting 
our continued focus on first-time buyers of health insurance and selecting a more healthier 
pool. The growth during the quarter was led by both volume and value, with the number of 
new-to-insurance policies growing over 10% year-on-year and the average sum insured also 
rising 13% year-on-year.  
 
A brief note getting into financial numbers: From this quarter, we have discontinued the 
practice of recognition of insurance finance charges. The previous periods have also 
accordingly been restated for comparability. There is no impact of this treatment on 
profitability metrics such as PAT and underwriting results.  
 
Now coming to the underwriting result for the quarter was Rs. 99 crore compared to a loss of 
Rs. 40 crore in Quarter 2 of last financial year. This is a positive swing of about Rs. 139 crore. 
For H1 FY27, our underwriting results stood at Rs. 210 crore as against a loss of Rs. 24 crore in 
H1 of FY26, giving a positive swing of Rs. 234 crore for H1. The underwriting results for H1 FY27 
surpassed the full-year FY26 underwriting result of Rs. 198 crore.  
 
The Combined Insurance Service Ratio, CISR, improved by 2.9% to 98% in Quarter 2 FY27 and 
by 2.4% to 97.9% for H1 of FY27. The profit after tax for the quarter increased over threefold 
to Rs. 265 crore from Rs. 80 crore in the last year same quarter. And the PAT for the half year 
increased by 57% year-on-year to Rs. 815 crore.  
 
To provide the right perspective on profitability insulated from short-term mark-to-market 
volatility, we report the normalized PAT pegged at a normalized annual investment yield of 8%. 
Under the normalized framework, our profit after tax for Quarter 2 increased 70% year-on-
year to Rs. 390 crore. The profit after tax for H1 increased 56% year-on-year to Rs. 775 crore, 
with a normalized ROE on annualized basis increasing from 11.2% of last year's H1 FY26 to 
15.1% ROE in H1 FY27.  
 
On the business side, we continue to build a diversified and granular retail franchise with 
disciplined and prudent risk selection across geographies, segments, channels, and products 
that meet our defined ROE threshold. Our Retail Health market share stood at 29% for H1 FY27 
and 30% for the quarter. As highlighted earlier, the reported market share continues to be 
influenced by the share of long-term policies and the consequent 1/n reporting and like-for-
like comparability will be restored only by FY28.  
 
More fundamentally, our scale reflects our deliberate focus on preferred segments and our 
conscious avoidance of riskier pools. Our proprietary channels, agency and digital D2C,

contributed over 90% of our retail business, giving us greater control over customer selection, 
quality of sales, and the economics of acquisition. We added 39,000 new agents during H1 
FY27, taking our network to 8.7 lakh agents. 
 
Our agency productivity improved by 19% year-on-year during H1. The agency continues to 
deepen penetration where it matters most, with fresh business growth from semi-urban and 
rural geographies at over 3 times that of metro and urban geographies. Our proprietary digital 
D2C channel remains the fastest growing, with 137% year-on-year growth in H1, led by younger 
customers, higher sum insured levels, and rising participation from non-metro and tier 2 
markets. Our D2C channel continues to have superior combined ratios.  
 
Beyond our proprietary channels, Bancassurance and alternate channels remain focused on 
profitable segments, while our group SME business through our agency network remains our 
priority within this segment.  
 
Our sustained trajectory of underwriting profitability reflects the rigorous execution of core 
levers that we have deployed which is enhanced risk selection, portfolio optimization towards 
preferred segments, and our risk-based pricing strategy, our robust mitigation of fraud, waste, 
and abuse, and the scaling up of our wellness-focused consumer ecosystem.  
 
In a seasonally demanding quarter, as you all know, the Quarter 2, our expanded home 
healthcare and telemedicine capabilities gained significant traction and served as a critical 
mechanism to manage our fever and infection-related cases.  
 
Our customer-focused metrics continue to demonstrate improvement. Our retail claim 
settlement ratio increased by over 1% to 92.4% for H1 FY27. Our renewal ratio improved by 4% 
to 102%. Overall company-level NPS also improved by 4 points to 65 as of September 2026. We 
settled 22.5 lakh claims during the first half of this year and 83% of those claims were settled 
on a cashless mode, which is probably the highest in the industry.  
 
Digital and AI remain central to our long-term growth strategy, serving as key drivers of 
operating leverage and productivity. During the quarter, we upgraded our core customer 
relationship management platform to Salesforce. This upgrade optimizes our D2C acquisition 
by enhancing the lead management precision and conversion. We have also scaled up 
deployment of AI bots across both our customer acquisition and service channels. Initial trends 
are highly encouraging. The bots processed over 7.5 million minutes of call volume while 
operating at less than 20% of the cost of equivalent human deployment.  
 
To further refine our digital acquisition strategy, we scaled our AI-driven quality assurance 
capabilities, analyzing over 10 million minutes of customer interaction across 9 languages. 
Concurrently, our service bots operated autonomously, independently resolving over 1,000 
customer interactions per day. On the distribution side, ecosystem engagement on our

proprietary ATOM Pro platform continued to deepen, with more than 50% of our active agents 
are utilizing the platform.  
 
In underwriting and claims, our partnership with Amplify Health has gone live with automation 
of FWA capabilities. Sharper analytics is increasingly refining our risk selection and claims 
decision, and our detection of fraud, waste, and abuse has been considerably strengthened 
across billing, tariff, and medical necessity parameters. Our analytics capabilities rest on 
extensive proprietary data, which remains an enduring competitive advantage for Star Health.  
 
Details of our operational and financial performance are provided in our quarterly update 
presentation, which is available on the stock exchanges and on our website as well. We would 
request you to refer to it for a more detailed analysis.  
 
Now let me come to the second part of my remarks, our preparation for H2 and beyond. As we 
enter the second half, last year's GST-led growth becomes part of the base, and headline 
growth rates will start to normalize for the industry as well as for Star Health. What matters 
most is the quality and durability of our operating performance, and we believe it is structurally 
sound and resilient for the following reasons:  
 
First, our underwriting performance is anchored in the strength of our vintage book, which 
accounts for about 80% of our portfolio. The improvement in our underwriting performance 
began in Quarter 2 of FY26, well before the GST-led growth set in, and it has now sustained for 
5 successive quarters. This is the outcome of prudent management of the entire portfolio 
through risk-based pricing, better portfolio selection through our data and analytics, and our 
highly efficient claims processing and FWA savings, our provider relationship and our 
negotiation with them, and also the strong wellness program that we run for our customers.  
 
Second, the share of the multi-year policies in our portfolio has risen steadily over the last few 
quarters. Premium on these policies is earned over the term of the contract, and a growing 
portion of our future earned premium is already contracted. This lends visibility and stability 
to our earned revenue base, while multi-tenure policies also strengthen persistency.  
 
Third, our growth engine is proprietary. We continue to add agents and expand our distribution 
network at a very consistent pace, deepening our presence in semi-urban and rural markets, 
and at the same time scaling our D2C channel amongst the digitally native segments such as 
the younger customers and salaried professionals. More than 9 in 10 of our fresh customers 
are new to insurance, drawn from preferred geographies and segments. This is the profile of a 
franchise that expands the market rather than one dependent on an external catalyst alone.  
 
We therefore enter H2 from a position of strength and confidence. The GST exemption 
demonstrated how strongly affordability unlocks demand for retail health insurance, 
particularly amongst the first-time buyers. We believe the distribution reforms proposed by 
the authority represent the next lever of affordability.

This brings me to the third part of my remarks, our perspective on the recent regulatory 
developments. The IRDAI has set out an ambitious reform agenda for the sector over the past 
few months, and let me touch upon the key developments. We welcome the proposed Public 
Insurance Registry envisaged as a digital public infrastructure for insurance by enabling 
policyholders, insurers, and other participants to discover, verify, and exchange information in 
a consistent manner.  
 
The PIR can meaningfully reduce information asymmetry, strengthen underwriting controls, 
simplify claims processing, and strengthen fraud detection across the ecosystem. It marks a 
decisive step towards a more transparent and efficient insurance market, and we look forward 
to participating in its development.  
 
Turning to the IRDAI's consultation paper, Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution, 
released on 23rd September, on which we have already submitted our views to the authority. 
At the outset, we welcome the direction of the proposed reforms and support the intent of 
better outcomes for customers. The framework envisaged in the paper is closely aligned with 
the distribution model that Star Health has built over 2 decades. We are prepared to meet the 
new requirements and play our part to contribute meaningfully towards the national ambition 
of insurance for all by 2047.  
 
Our core business model is very resilient, with over 90% of our retail business being sourced 
through proprietary channels. Individual agents remain the better rewarded distributors under 
the proposed framework, and we are engaging closely with our agents to sustain and enhance 
their earnings through higher productivity.  
 
As commercials cease to be a differentiator, insurers will increasingly focus on the strength of 
the product and the product proposition, claims experience, service and brand, and 
distribution, in which we believe we are very strongly positioned. Several other proposals are 
also encouraging quoting commissions aligned to renewal rates removes incentive for 
commission-driven churn between insurers, which we see happening in large numbers as you 
know. This shift will encourage insurers to expand insurance penetration by enrolling new 
customers as against market cannibalization through higher commissions. 
 
Equally, the proposed higher commissions for smaller towns and rural areas and the 
requirement that an agent represents only one insurer with a product segment are well aligned 
with our distribution footprint.  
 
Our internal estimates indicate a credible path to the proposed expense of management limits 
as a combination of prudent management, operating leverage, and productivity enhancements 
through our digitization and automation initiatives. Star Health has a consistent track record of 
demonstrating compliance with EOM requirements and is committed to maintaining that 
standard in the future as well.

We are cognizant of the authority's sharp focus on dark patterns in digital journeys and we fully 
share the emphasis on consumer trust. As digital channels account for a growing share of how 
consumers buy and service their policies, we continue to review our digital journeys and will 
ensure full alignment with the evolving framework. We believe that consent-led data 
collection, transparent access to product features and pricing, and clear disclosures will over 
time reinforce the advantage of trusted and direct brands.  
 
Our comments pertain to the consultation paper in its current form, and we await the final 
regulations. In the evolving paradigm, our advantage rests on a principle that is central to the 
paper, which is dedicated distribution, which builds lasting customer relationships and is 
rewarded appropriately.  
 
With that, we come to the end of our opening remarks. I once again thank you for your 
continued trust in Star Health, and I look forward to your questions. Thank you so much.
